name: SharePoint
description: Let agents work with files and Excel spreadsheets in the SharePoint sites you add, and look up people in your organization. Agents have no OneDrive of their own: a person's OneDrive is a site too, reached only if you add it and give the app access to it.
identity: Your Microsoft app registration, through the Microsoft connection. It reaches only the files and spreadsheets in the sites you give it, unless you choose all sites, read-only.

setup.title: Add these Microsoft Graph permissions to the app
setup.body: In the app, open API permissions, select Add a permission, then Microsoft Graph, then Application permissions, and add exactly these. Sites.Selected reaches only the sites you give the app, one by one. Unless you choose all sites, read-only, do not add Sites.Read.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All or Files.Read.All: they reach every site and file in your organization.
copy: az ad app permission add --id {clientId} --api 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000 --api-permissions "$(az ad sp show --id 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000 --query "appRoles[?value=='{scope}'].id" -o tsv)=Role"
click: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Entra ID, then App registrations, and open {brand.microsoft.appName}.
Select API permissions, then Add a permission, then Microsoft Graph, then Application permissions.

setup.title: Grant admin consent
setup.body: Still under API permissions, select "Grant admin consent". This needs a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator, and is needed again whenever you add a permission. Each permission should then show Granted. With Commands, a permission that was granted already is answered with "Permission being assigned already exists", which is fine.
click: Still under API permissions, select Grant admin consent for your organization, then Yes.
Each permission should show Granted under Status.
copy: SP=$(az ad sp show --id {clientId} --query id -o tsv)

az rest --method post --url "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/$SP/appRoleAssignments" --body "{\"principalId\": \"$SP\", \"resourceId\": \"$GRAPH\", \"appRoleId\": \"$(az ad sp show --id 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000 --query "appRoles[?value=='{scope}'].id" -o tsv)\"}"

fields.label: Which sites the app can reach

options.label: Only the sites you give it
options.description: Recommended. The app reaches a site only after it is given access to that site.

options.label: All sites, read-only
options.description: The app can read every site and every person's OneDrive in your organization, files and spreadsheets alike, with no grant per site. Each API key still reaches only the sites and folders you choose for it. To let agents add files or edit spreadsheets in a site, give the app write access to that site as well.

capabilities.label: Read files
capabilities.description: List and read files in the sites you add, and only those.
capabilities.forbidden: Microsoft refused this. An administrator has to give the app read access to this site (the SharePoint page in {brand.productName} shows the command). A new grant can take a few minutes to apply.

capabilities.label: Read spreadsheets
capabilities.description: List Excel workbooks, their sheets and tables, and read cells in the sites you add.
capabilities.forbidden: Microsoft refused this. An administrator has to give the app read access to this site (the SharePoint page in {brand.productName} shows the command). A new grant can take a few minutes to apply.

capabilities.label: Add and change files
capabilities.description: Add files to those sites and replace existing ones. The app needs write access to each of them, not read.
capabilities.forbidden: Microsoft refused this. Adding or changing files needs the app to have write access to this site; a site given read access only refuses changes. The SharePoint page in {brand.productName} shows the command. A new grant can take a few minutes to apply.

capabilities.label: Edit spreadsheets
capabilities.description: Change cells and add rows to tables in those workbooks. The app needs write access to each of those sites, not read.
capabilities.forbidden: Microsoft refused this. Editing spreadsheets needs the app to have write access to this site; a site given read access only refuses changes. The SharePoint page in {brand.productName} shows the command. A new grant can take a few minutes to apply.

capabilities.label: Read users and groups
capabilities.description: Look up people's names, email addresses and job titles, and list group members.
capabilities.note: Reaches everyone in your organization, not just chosen sites. Read-only. Leave it off unless agents need to look people up.
capabilities.forbidden: Microsoft refused this. The app needs {scopes} with admin consent.

limits.label: Sites
limits.help: The sites whose files and spreadsheets this key may use, from the sites the app can open. It can use no others.

limits.label: Folder
limits.help: Optional, for each site: the one folder this key may use there, for files and spreadsheets alike, such as Contracts/Signed. Leave it empty for the whole site.

grant.title: With Microsoft Graph PowerShell
grant.body: Run by a SharePoint or Global Administrator.
copy: # Needs Microsoft Graph PowerShell: Install-Module Microsoft.Graph -Scope CurrentUser
New-MgSitePermission -SiteId $site.Id -BodyParameter @{ roles = @('{site_role}'); grantedToIdentities = @(@{ application = @{ id = '{clientId}'; displayName = "{brand.microsoft.appName}" } }) }

grant.title: Or raise a site the app already reads
grant.body: A site given read access refuses changes. To let agents add files or edit spreadsheets there, change that grant to write.
copy: # Needs Microsoft Graph PowerShell: Install-Module Microsoft.Graph -Scope CurrentUser

verify.label: Microsoft permissions the app has
verify.ifEmpty: The app has no Microsoft Graph application permissions yet. Add the permissions above and grant admin consent.

discover.label: Sites agents can use
discover.ifEmpty: No sites yet. Add the sites agents may use below.

revoke: Remove the app's access to each site (Remove-MgSitePermission), or remove its Sites.Selected and Sites.Read.All permissions. To stop every Microsoft app at once, remove the app registration (see the Microsoft connection).
